title: Nick Betts Recounts Alleged Area 51 Reptilian Shootout — Liberation Times
excerpt: Nick Betts shares a secondhand account of an alleged deadly reptilian encounter near Area 51, echoing David Grusch’s claims on Joe Rogan.
content:
Written by Christopher Sharp - 15 October 2026

Former U.S. Army sniper Nick Betts recounted an alleged deadly encounter with reptilian-looking beings on the Liberty Risk podcast, released on 5 December 2025. 

Betts said an unnamed man who claimed to have taken part in the operation told him that U.S. personnel had entered an underground installation near Area 51, killed three beings and lost one of their own men.

Betts heard the story in a hotel room in Poland. He had been travelling through Eastern Europe to film a documentary about the war in Ukraine, alongside a friend who had served in a Ranger battalion, the storyteller, an older man and another companion.

According to Betts, the storyteller and the older man had served together in the same squadron and both participated in the alleged operation. The older man was asleep elsewhere when the story was told.

Betts and his friend, whom he called ‘Ranger’, were downloading footage in their shared hotel room when the storyteller arrived with four bottles of wine. Ranger brought up aliens and asked what the man knew.

The man initially refused to answer. After further prompting, he collected their phones and placed them in a microwave, which Betts described as an improvised Faraday cage intended to block electronic signals.

He then described an alleged deployment years earlier, while serving in an unnamed squadron at Fort Bragg. The installation is home to Delta Force’s squadrons and includes Pope Army Airfield, where the U.S. Air Force’s 24th and 21st Special Tactics Squadrons are based. 

Betts referred to Joint Special Operations Command, or JSOC, during his account, but did not identify the squadron or either alleged participant.

The squadron had been on quick reaction force duty. A quick reaction force, or QRF, is held ready to respond rapidly to an emergency. It describes a role rather than a particular unit; military accounts describe infantry, Rangers and Marines performing such duties.

The storyteller said he had been at a bar when the recall came. Personnel were ordered back to base, told to collect their equipment and put on an aircraft without being briefed on their destination or mission - it was added that this was highly abnormal.

A few hours later, they landed in intense heat. Two men met them outside a hangar, brought them inside and took them to a Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility, or SCIF, a secure facility for handling sensitive intelligence.

There, they were allegedly told:

“Gentlemen. Welcome to Area 51.”

The mission briefing followed. Security personnel at an underground installation a few miles away had stopped conducting their regular radio checks. A QRF had already been sent to investigate, but that team had also fallen silent.

The personnel flown in from Bragg were therefore the second QRF dispatched to the installation. According to Betts, they were tasked with entering the facility and requested and received a map and a plan for getting in and out.

Before departing, they asked to check their firearms’ sights at a range. They were told they would not need those guns and were instead issued unfamiliar weapons that did not take magazines. Betts described them as “a high-energy weapon system”.

A Black Hawk helicopter took them to the entrance. They descended through a tunnel and entered a long hallway leading to a T-junction and a horseshoe-shaped passage. The storyteller described a strong, sewer-like smell.

As the team moved around the curved passage, the serviceman on its outer, left-hand side was allegedly struck in the chest by a weapon of the same kind they had been issued. He was killed, and the surviving personnel returned fire.

According to Betts’s retelling, the attacker walked on two legs, looked mildly reptilian, had fingers and was carrying the weapon. The team had allegedly been told there were three beings inside the installation and killed all three.

Asked later in the podcast how many personnel had entered, Betts said the storyteller had not supplied a headcount. He guessed six. 

The storyteller claimed the dead serviceman’s body was cremated immediately. His colleagues allegedly objected because he was Catholic and cremation went against his beliefs. Betts separately said the team had been prevented from taking the body home in a casket, with sterilisation given as the reason it had to remain at the site. His death was said to have been recorded as a training accident.

The surviving personnel allegedly signed documents, had their identification photographed and underwent further biometric scans.

Betts acknowledged that the storyteller had been drinking, telling the hosts:

“He was drunk, but he wasn’t fucking sloppy.”

What happened the next morning, Betts said, was why he took the account seriously.

The group was due to meet in the hotel lobby in the morning. On his way downstairs, Betts encountered the older man whom the storyteller had identified as another participant in the operation.

Betts casually mentioned that their mutual companion had said the older man knew something about aliens.

The man immediately grabbed him by the neck and slammed him against a wall, Betts alleged. He warned Betts never to discuss the subject again, then demanded to know where he had heard the story.

Betts later saw the two men arguing. The storyteller subsequently confronted him and demanded that he leave the country. Betts said neither man would speak to him for the remainder of the trip.

Betts said the fallout cost him the documentary job. He and Ranger were told to pack after breakfast, and he recalled hiding beneath bedsheets and pillows while calling his wife to say he was coming home early.

“I literally got canned off the job,” he said.

He and Ranger were then taken to a facility Betts described as a “black site”, driven to an airport and flown home from Poland. On the flight, he asked Ranger what he made of the incident. His friend replied:

“I think you shut the fuck up about it.”

The hosts suggested the story and confrontation could have been a prank. Betts questioned why a joke would end with him losing his job and thousands of dollars in paid work.

He also acknowledged that discussing the account publicly made him nervous. Asked whether one of the men would be angry to hear him recount it, he replied:

“That’s why I’m nervous.”

His account was published nearly ten months before David Grusch’s appearance on The Joe Rogan Experience on 30 September 2026.

Grusch, the former Air Force intelligence officer who testified before Congress in July 2023, told Rogan that his contacts had described reptilian-looking beings, some more than seven feet tall, with scaly skin and a gorilla-like appearance. He added that others were described as more humanoid in appearance.

He alleged that U.S. personnel had shot living reptilian beings during a crash retrieval, and that Americans had been injured and killed. Asked why the beings were shot, Grusch said:

“It posed a threat.”

Betts and Grusch are not alone in relaying claims about reptilian-looking beings.

In May 2025, Dr Eric W. Davis, a theoretical physicist and former Pentagon contractor, told lawmakers during a multi-panel event that his sources had described beings resembling reptiles among the crews of some UFOs.

Separately, an intelligence community source speaking to Liberation Times described alleged reptile-like beings referred to as “strangers”.

The source described them as aggressive beings based beneath the Moon’s surface and claimed they were competing with a “Nordic” group characterised as more empathetic.

The source did not describe a conventional war:

“Competition between the sides may be nearly as old as humanity itself. What I've heard described isn't an outright war, but rather a scaled-down adversarial relationship.

“It's unclear which sides have aligned with international governments, or which sides are cooperating with factions within the program. It's quite possible that every government has had to manage this competition among the sides.”

The account echoes Grusch’s broader claims on The Joe Rogan Experience of conflict between different non-human groups.
